So right now I'm playing Curse of the Azure Bonds parallel with Baldur's Gate. So that's a 1989 RPG and a 1998 RPG. I'm sort of comparing and contrasting the various design decisions they made. Last year I played Pool of Radiance and I'm pretty sure I enjoyed that a lot more than Curse of the Azure Bonds.

I do find I enjoy the core gameplay loop of the Gold Box games a lot more than the Infinity Engine games. I love the first person exploration, and the separate shift to a tactical combat screen when you encounter enemies. The turn based combat is also far superior to the Infinity Engine, and the grid it takes place on makes aiming fireball and other AOE spells infinitely easier and more accurate.

Comparing Pool of Radiance to Baldur's Gate, I much more enjoyed Pool of Radiance. However, I think I'm enjoying Curse of the Azure Bonds a lot less than Baldur's Gate.

It comes down to a few issues. Pool of Radiance had a huge array of tactical nuts to crack. Trolls that wouldn't stay down, enemies that could instantly "kill" you with poison. Your magic user mostly stayed on crowd control duty with Sleep spells and the like. Moving into the sequel, the combat becomes a rather one trick pony. Lots of magic resistant or immune enemies that cast Hold Person on your entire party. You either succeed in your saving throw against it, or you get taken down immediately. Nothing else tends to be remotely difficult. Crowd control is mostly useless since everything you'd want to use it on is immune.

It wouldn't be so frustrating if half the time you encounter these stupid Hold Person casting enemies and you ended up needing to reload your game, you could just do that. But you can't. You either need to wait for the encounter to play itself out and have everyone die, or you need to restart the game. There is no load feature in the normal menus. In that respect, Infinity Engine games let me iterate on failure much faster, and as a result are far less frustrating.

At this point I'm tuning out of trying to find and do everything in Curse of the Azure Bonds like I did with Pool of Radiance. I may just try to rush to the end in as quick a line as possible. We'll see.
